_comment: THE CONVERSATIONAL LOOP — PLAN 2x §3.3. The AI writes this file and bumps `rev`; the Texture panel polls /api/textureparams once a second and regenerates on a rev change. No websocket, no connection state, survives a page reload. `autoplay` is absent BY DESIGN — sound only ever on the composer's SPACE or Play. Every label must NAME THE DIALS IT MOVED (§6's two-sided contract), so the qualitative interface never goes opaque.
_slate: rev 5 (2026-08-20, day 21) - rev 2 UNTOUCHED (A-F = the smear tempo ladder the composer kept) + variant G appended: THE ACCRETION STEP-UP, the composer pairing spoken aloud - 4 players at C tempo, 6 at D, 8 at E, 10 at F - as ONE continuous 24 s gesture (6 s per step, gap 0; the engine default gap of 2 would insert silence). Players and tempo climb together, so composite rate goes 4.8 -> 9 -> 14.4 -> 22 per s, steeper than tempo alone. Free-form player browsing needs NO new variant: the panel players field regenerates on edit (resets to the file value on variant switch by design). rev numbering: 3 was the character x speed grid, 4 the six ladder-gestures; both in git. || rev 8 (2026-08-20, day 21): LIVE block for PLAN 2ag - the live rig (composer approved option a: gallop folded in via dBpm; auto-run included). Five sequences, each = jitterMs + dBpm + root + six (bpm,players) steps. The panel reads this block on every rev bump - AI writes land in the open panel within ~1 s, PROVEN LIVE this sitting (rev-7 probe: slot jump + bpm 61 observed in the boxes with no reload). Composer box edits are ephemeral until asked to be persisted here. S1-S3 = the kept A-F rungs in smear / rain (jit 45) / gallop (d2); S4 = extended accretion (players AND bpm climb, 4.8 -> 22/s); S5 = scratch. rev 6/7 were the uncommitted build + probe states. || rev 10 (2026-08-20, day 21): PHASE LADDER (composer-approved design, this sitting). New per-step number: offset (the rotor - player j at (j x offset) mod 1 of the per-player cycle; 0 = legacy even round-robin). Step count now follows the file (steps are rows in the panel grid). S6 phase = the first-pass 12-rung complexity ladder at fixed 108 BPM x 10: 0.1 even reference / 0.5 two pulse-stacks / 0.33333333 three / 0.25 four / 0.2 five pairs / 0.125 eight-grid accents / 0.0625 phrase+rest / 0.1875 sixteen-grid figure / 0.15 twenty-grid figure / 0.6180339887 golden lumpy / 0.03 wide cascade / 0.01 tightest decollage (mock-up-only precision - the ~30-50 ms stage/human floor applies live). Refine by asking - the AI rewrites the rungs, boxes follow within a second. Part 2 (the dialed 6-step stopwatch run) uses the same machinery once the composer names keepers. || rev 11 (2026-08-20, day 21): S6 phase = THE ZONE COMPLEXITY LADDER (composer chose the 1/2 -> 1/3 zone). The two-axis finding, composer-heard: offset AMOUNT and RATIO COMPLEXITY are independent; rev 10 walked amounts at mostly-simple ratios. This ladder holds the ZONE fixed and walks DEPTH via the mediant (Stern-Brocot) sequence: 1/2, 2/5, 3/7, 4/9, 5/12, 7/17, limit sqrt(2)-1 (the zone noble). Measured group counts 2/5/7/9/10/10/10 - pulse fissions into figure into lump; rungs 5-7 differ by GRID (12/17/never), an ear distinction not a count one. Fixed 108 BPM x 10, jitter 0. Other zones (around 1/3, 1/4) = future slates on request. || rev 12: composer read the zone ladder as not running the gamut - correct, by design (zone fixed, depth walked). Fix: BOTH AXES AS SLOTS. S6 phase = the zone/complexity walk unchanged; S7 amount = the rev-10 full-gamut amount ladder restored (0.1 even / 0.5 / 1-3 / 0.25 / 0.2 / 0.125 / 0.0625 / 0.1875 / 0.15 / golden / 0.03 / 0.01). Landing stays on phase. || rev 13: composer correctly caught that the mediant walk CONVERGES to ~0.414 rather than SWEEPING 1/2 -> 1/3 as stated. S6 phase rewritten as the actual sweep: all zone fractions with q<=12 in descending value order - 1/2, 5/11, 4/9, 3/7, 5/12, 2/5, 3/8, 4/11, 1/3. Complexity necessarily zigzags along a value-ordered sweep (group counts 2/10/9/7/10/5/8/10/3); the readout names each rung count. || rev 14: THE COMPUTED COMPLEXITY LADDER (the experiment the composer approved). 997 offsets scored at 98 BPM x 10 (pattern = fusion-merged onset groups at 25 ms; score = gap CV + 0.1 x stack-size std) -> 430 distinct audible patterns -> 12 picks with MONOTONE rising score 0.00 -> 1.25. Characters: 1 two pulses / 2 five pulses / 3 seven with accents / 4 seven with a limp / 5 near-smear with one hitch / 6 lilting 51-62 swing / 7 three-gap cell / 8-9 nine-run + long holes / 10 sharp 33-112 cell / 11 tight run + two big holes / 12 fast ripple + 290 ms rest. Scorer: scratchpad score_offsets.js (also in the running log). The composer LISTENS for monotonicity - where two rungs sound alike or out of order, that corrects the scoring weights. || rev 15: FIRST EAR DATA on the phase arc. Composer verdict on rev 14 (verbatim in RUNNING_LOG/PAPER_NOTES): the process is by nature DISCURSIVE - dramatic changes - and the U is audible in the produced series; for the piece the composer wants a smooth ramp. New slot try1 = the composer own order of rev-14 rungs 11-2-7-3-10-4-6 (score path 0.77/0.00/0.34/0.05/0.58/0.09/0.29 - an alternating high-low, i.e. playing WITH the dramatic-change quality). The phase slot stays UNTOUCHED as the reference series - rung numbers 1-12 remain the working identifiers. || rev 16: try1 step-swaps per composer (2<->3, 4<->5): rung order now 11-7-2-10-3-4-6. || rev 17: try1 steps 4<->5 reverted: 11-7-2-3-10-4-6. || rev 18: try1 = composer cut step 5 (rung 10) and asked the max playable tempo for the final step - at unison C3 the cap is offset-INDEPENDENT (rotor moves phases, not per-player rates): 60/ring(C3 0.42s) = 142.9, measured clean at 140/dirty at 143; top set to 140 for margin. Ramp 95 -> 140 in equal 9-BPM steps across the six rungs 11-7-2-3-10dropped-4-6 -> 11-7-2-3-4-6. Rotor characters survive re-tempo (patterns scale with the cycle). || rev 19: try1 ramp re-spanned 87 -> 120 (equal 6.6-BPM steps), same rungs 11-7-2-3-4-6. || rev 20: (a) SEQUENCE SAVED - live.saved[] gets phaseSeq-01, a frozen copy of try1 as kept by the composer 2026-08-20 (rungs 11-7-2-3-4-6, ramp 87->120, unison C3); the working try1 slot stays editable. (b) PITCH PRESETS in the live rig - new pitch dropdown: unison / octaves (root pc, 30-65) / fifths stack / cluster F-A octave spread [30,31,33,41,42,44,45,53,55,57] (F1=29 is below the staccato floor, so the bottom octave starts at F#1). Lane j = pitches[j], ascending across the stage. Measured per-player ring caps: unison 142 / octaves 125 / fifths 122 / clusterFA 117 - the readout warns per set; NOTE try1 tops at 120, which exceeds the clusterFA cap at the last step (mock-up plays it cleanly; the hall would not).
